findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The PR replaces loginTotpStep1 in the Lithuanian file with the Italian sentence "Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:" instead of a Lithuanian translation. Lithuanian users on the TOTP setup page will see Italian text. The same wrong-language text was also put into themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties line 101 (totpStep1). Both should be Lithuanian, e.g. "Įdiekite vieną iš šių programėlių savo mobiliajame telefone:".

findings.title: error-invalid-multivalued-size now uses Java MessageFormat choice syntax that the JS UI cannot render
findings.body: The account UI (and the admin UI in js/apps/admin-ui/maven-resources-community/theme/keycloak.v2/admin/messages/messages_en.properties line 3138, same change) is a React app using i18next-style interpolation with double braces (the previous value used {{0}}, {{1}}, {{2}}). The new value uses single braces {0} and a Java ChoiceFormat pattern {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}. i18next does not understand Java ChoiceFormat and single braces are not the interpolation syntax there, so users will see the raw literal string "Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}." instead of a formatted message. This key should keep the {{n}} placeholders and plain wording in the JS theme files; the choice format is only valid for the server-side FreeMarker/Java themes (themes/src/main/resources...).

findings.title: Missing English properties file crashes the build with a RuntimeException instead of being reported/skipped
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() derives the English file path via string replaceAll("resources-community","resources") plus a regex renaming the locale suffix to _en, then opens it with FileInputStream and throws a bare RuntimeException if it is missing. Any message file for which that derived path does not exist (e.g. a locale file with no messages_en.properties sibling, or a path where the 'resources-community' → 'resources' mapping does not hold, such as the js/ maven-resources theme trees) will abort the mojo with an unhandled RuntimeException rather than produce a MojoExecutionException or a recorded verification message. This also breaks the existing contract of verify(), which only declares MojoExecutionException and collects problems into the message list.

findings.title: santizeAnchors removes the first occurrence of an anchor, not the matched one, and only checks pairwise order
findings.body: When a translation contains the same anchor text more than once, value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "") deletes the first occurrence in the string, which may not be the occurrence the matcher found (earlier identical anchors may already have been removed at different positions, or an English anchor may appear before the matched one). This can silently leave a disallowed anchor in the value that then passes the policy check, or produce misleading 'Didn't find anchor tag' reports when the translation reorders anchors relative to English. The removal should target the index of the current matcher match (matcher.start()/end()), and the comparison should be order-independent or explicitly documented as order-sensitive.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese file gets Traditional Chinese text for totpStep1
findings.body: The new totpStep1 value in messages_zh_CN.properties is written in Traditional Chinese ("在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：" using 機/裝/應用程式) while this is the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) resource. Simplified users expect 在您的手机上安装以下应用之一：. The Traditional variant belongs in messages_zh_TW.properties.

findings.title: containsHtml only matches lowercase tags, so mixed-case English tags disable the HTML allowance
findings.body:
HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>") only recognizes lowercase tag names. If an English source value ever contains an uppercase or mixed-case tag (e.g.
or ), containsHtml() returns false and the policy degrades to POLICY_NO_HTML for that key, so legitimate translations carrying the same tag would be flagged as illegal HTML (false positive) — or conversely the check silently diverges from what the sanitizer allows. A case-insensitive match ([a-zA-Z]) would be more robust.
